title: Chainsaw thigh - woods extraction
objectives: Tourniquet within 1 min of reaching pt; 2nd TQ if bleeding persists
Note & communicate TQ time; never loosen
Resource management for remote extraction (FD, UTV, LZ)
Hemorrhagic shock: permissive 250 mL boluses, warm
TRAUMA ALERT: active bleeding requiring TQ = Level 1 criteria
resources: CAT TQ x2, hemostatic gauze, IV, NS, blankets, Stokes/sked, FD UTV. Pt 1/4 mi from road; UVMMC (Level 1) ~20 min from road
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to the end of Pleasant Valley Rd, Underhill, logging operation, for a 52-year-old male with a chainsaw injury to the leg, heavy bleeding. Caller is a coworker. Fire is also responding. Time out 1030.

scene.location: Logging site, 1/4 mile up skid trail from road. 35 F, mud, slash piles.
scene.setup: Pt on ground against log. Coworker holding bloody shirt on wound + leather belt around thigh (loose).
scene.moulage: Large lac R anterior mid-thigh, chaps cut through, blood-soaked pants, puddle.
scene.roles: Pt actor; coworker (bystander - later asks to loosen TQ); FD arrives T+10.

patient.name: Dale Corbett
patient.on_arrival: Pale, sweaty, anxious, talking. Bright red blood pulsing through shirt. Belt not controlling it.

SAMPLE: Saw kicked back at 1015 limbing a tree. Coworker applied belt

primary: **Arterial bleeding R thigh - TQ high & tight / 2-3 in above wound**
Radial weak/thready. Pale, cool, diaphoretic. ~1.5 L on ground
GCS 15 -> trends down if bleeding uncontrolled
Cut away pants; only wound. Cold, wet ground - insulate
**HIGH**: class III hemorrhage. TQ, warm, move
secondary: 8 in gaping lac anterior/medial mid-thigh, muscle exposed
After TQ: no DP/PT pulses, bleeding stopped

vitals.trigger: IF single TQ not tight / belt only (~T+5)
vitals.other: Oozing past TQ, distal pulse present -> tighten / 2nd TQ

flow.give: Coworker waving from skid trail: "Hurry, he's bleeding bad!"
expected: Carry minimal gear fast: TQ, gauze, O2, BVM
FD carry team + UTV requested early

flow.give: Show WOUND card. Belt loose, blood pulsing.

branches.if: TQ high & tight / 2-3 in proximal, tightened

expected.text: TQ applied <= 1 min of reaching pt

flow.give: If one TQ: some ooze continues at +3 min (big thigh).

expected.text: Insulated from ground, wet clothes cut off

flow.give: Coworker: "Shouldn't you loosen that? He'll lose his leg!"
expected: TQ left in place; coworker reassured
IV / fluids started en route or at road
Pain addressed (2.20A: AEMT options; intercept for opioids)

flow.give: FD arrives with UTV + Stokes at T+10. Stage **D** if not warmed.
expected: CC directs carry-out, keeps eyes on TQ

branches.if: TQ #1 slips during carry; bleeding resumes
branches.then: Stage **B** values; expect stop, tighten/2nd TQ, re-mark time

branches.if: UTV stuck in mud: hand carry 1/4 mi
branches.then: CC rotates FD carriers, keeps TQ visible, keeps pt warm

flow.give: Stage **E**. Evaluator plays UVMMC trauma team.
expected: Report: TQ time(s), est. blood loss, fluid total

critical: No TQ within 1 min of reaching pt with arterial bleeding
TQ placed loosely (distal pulse/bleeding persists) and not corrected
debrief: What should be the first thing out of the bag on this call?
Why a second TQ instead of loosening and re-applying?
How did you handle the coworker's push to loosen it?
What resources did you call, and when?
What is the lethal triad, and how did you address it?

crew_card.dispatch: End of Pleasant Valley Rd, Underhill, logging operation. 52 y/o M, chainsaw injury to leg, heavy bleeding. Caller: coworker. FD responding.
crew_card.on_arrival: Coworker waving you up a muddy skid trail. ~1/4 mile in: man sitting against a log, pants soaked red, coworker pressing a shirt on his thigh.

actor_card.Act: Pale, shaky, cold. Talk fast, scared. "Am I gonna lose my leg?"
actor_card.TQ tightened: Yell - it hurts more than the cut. Don't fight it.
actor_card.If bleeding not controlled: Get quiet and confused, eyes closing.
actor_card.Coworker at ~T+8: "Shouldn't you loosen that so his leg gets blood?" Push once, then accept explanation.
actor_card.Volunteer: Only if asked: "I take a baby aspirin every day."

show_cards.title: WOUND - R THIGH
show_cards.body:
8 in gash front/inside mid-thigh through chaps.
Bright red blood **pulsing**.
Belt above it, loose.

show_cards.title: R THIGH - REASSESS
show_cards.body:
Slow ooze from wound.
Faint pulse top of foot.
show_cards.cue: Give 3 min after a single TQ. If tightened / 2nd TQ placed: say bleeding stops, no distal pulse

show_cards.title: GROUND
show_cards.body: Blood pooled ~ size of a large dinner tray (~1.5 L) on mud and leaves.

moulage_tags.text: 8 in gash front/inside of thigh; bright red blood PULSING

moulage_tags.cue: Remove/flip once TQ is tight: no pulse

learn_more.topic: femoral artery hemorrhage from a chainsaw injury
learn_more.focus: tourniquet placement and conversion, second tourniquets, and preventing hypothermia in trauma (lethal triad)
